item.title: Reconstructing Ross Sea cryosphere–ocean variability during the Miocene Climatic Optimum using palynology
item.dc:creator: Suning Hou, Joseph G. Prebble, Evi Wubben, Laura De Santis, Robert M. McKay, Denise K. Kulhanek, … (+1)
item.description:
Journal of Micropalaeontology — matched: ice sheet, cryosphere, Antarctic, sea ice
The fate of the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) under climate warming remains highly debated. Geological evidence from the warm Miocene Climatic Optimum (MCO, ∼ 17–14.7 Ma) is still limited to a few circum-Antarctic records but generally suggests substantial AIS retreat and reduced or absent sea ice. Yet the magnitude and temporal variability of the cryosphere dynamics within the generally warm MCO remain poorly constrained. Here, we present a marine and terrestrial palynological record from sediments recovered at site U1521 on the outer shelf of the central Ross Sea during the International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) Expedition 374, spanning portions of the interval ∼ 17.3–14.5 Ma. Dinoflagellate cysts and freshwater-tolerant and brackish-water algae indicate variable surface ocean temperature, productivity and ice melting related to the transition from a marine-terminated ice sheet (16.3–16.2 Ma) to fully open-ocean peak warmth conditions (16.0 Ma). Terrestrial palynomorphs also indicate alternate cooling and warming phases on the hinterland, closely coupled to ice and ocean dynamics. Persistent vegetation implies continued (at least partially) ice-free terrestrial habitats. These results highlight substantial variability in AIS and ocean conditions during the MCO despite an overall warm climate state.

item.title: Spatial structure of diatom communities inhabiting Antarctic cryoconite holes
item.dc:creator: Raquel Viso, Jan Kollár, Kateřina Kopalová, Linda Nedbalová, Josef Elster, Flavia Dory, … (+4)
item.description:
Journal of Glaciology — matched: glacier, Antarctic, Antarctica
Cryoconite holes are water-filled depressions on glacier surfaces hosting a broad range of organisms, including diatoms. Yet, the biogeographic structure of these diatom communities has not been explored for the Antarctic Realm. Combining both light microscopy and rbcL metabarcoding, we investigated spatial variation in cryoconite diatom communities across two major Antarctic regions (i.e. Antarctic Peninsula and Continent), each represented by four additional subregions. Well-developed diatom communities were observed in most subregions, with species and genus richness comparable across sites, and molecular results generally in agreement with morphological observations at the genus level. A small number of taxa dominated, with six genera accounting for ~95% of all valves counted. Of these, Psammothidium and Humidophila were the most abundant and prevalent, while the genus Muelleria was common in, yet confined to, one subregion (McMurdo Dry Valleys). Beta-diversity analyses revealed clear differences in diatom community composition among regions and subregions. Notably, ~87% of all species were region-specific (81% on the Peninsula and 73% on the Continent), indicating pronounced spatial structure. Accordingly, our results suggest that the integration of dispersal limitation, environmental characteristics, and regional history influences cryoconite diatom community assembly at large spatial scales, and advance our understanding of microbial ecology within Antarctica.

item.title: An open-source tool for mapping key metrics of glacier health from space
item.dc:creator: Kara A. Lamantia, Laura J. Larocca, Rainey Aberle, Fabien Maussion, James M. Lea
item.description:
Journal of Glaciology — matched: glacier, firn, proxy, climate change
Satellite-based observations enable monitoring of glacier health metrics, essential for assessing glacier response to climate change and the environmental services they provide. Here, we present a Google Earth Engine tool for automated mapping of key climate- and mass balance- modulated parameters, including total visible ice area, snow-covered area (SCA), accumulation-area ratio, and snowline altitude (often used as a proxy for the equilibrium-line altitude). The tool uses Landsat near-infrared reflectance, commonly used spectral band ratios, and scene-specific thresholding to distinguish snow-covered from ice or firn surfaces. Validation for 60 glaciers across 13 regions shows strong agreement with manual observations of satellite imagery and weaker agreement with field-based observations from the World Glacier Monitoring Service (WGMS), likely reflecting differences in methodology and observation timing. The tool substantially improves WGMS temporal coverage, filling ~63% of glacier-year gaps and increasing the total number of observations (e.g., SCA by ~65%). Beyond the glaciers studied here, the tool is designed to enable efficient and accessible generation of multi-decadal glacier health time series for individual glaciers globally, with appropriate user evaluation and consideration of known limitations. Thus, the tool will hold value for a range of academic and non-academic users, particularly for education, outreach, and community stakeholders.

item.title: Meridional ocean temperature gradient drives climate stability in the Late Ordovician
item.dc:creator: Joseph Naar, Yannick Donnadieu, Alexandre Pohl, Guillaume Le Hir, Jean‐Baptiste Ladant, Daniel John Lunt
item.description:
Science Advances — matched: sea ice, proxy, model intercomparison, parameterization
The Hirnantian glaciation (Late Ordovician, 445 million years ago) involved rapid tropical cooling of ∼7°C, difficult to reproduce without invoking a major decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2). A previous modeling study provided an appealing explanation by identifying a climatic instability in the Late Ordovician ocean-atmosphere system using the Fast Ocean Atmosphere Model (FOAM), whereby a modest decrease in atmospheric partial pressure of CO 2 (P co 2) triggered abrupt tropical cooling. Here, our simulations with the comprehensive IPSL-CM5A2 model instead show continuous cooling as P co 2 decreases. We attribute this contrasting behavior to the warmer high-latitude climate simulated by FOAM, which predisposes sea ice to an abrupt transition and arises from overly diffusive ocean dynamics and coupled cloud radiative processes. Yet, broader model intercomparison suggests that climate stability is controlled by the equator-to-pole temperature gradient, rather than by model realism or complexity. These findings have major implications for constraining the onset and evolution of the Hirnantian glaciation, by exploiting proxy-constrained meridional temperature gradients and contrasting model parameterizations as physically motivated end-member hypotheses.

item.title: Seismic legacy effects on warming-induced damage evolution of glacier ice: event-constrained numerical simulations
item.dc:creator: Tian Zhang, Lin Wu, Xiaoqin Li, Prem Bahadur Thapa, Yuxiang Hu, Yu Lan, … (+8)
item.description:
Carbon Neutral Systems — matched: glacier, irreversible, numerical method
The 2026 Nepal–China mixed rock–ice avalanche raises questions about whether prior seismic disturbances may influence subsequent warming-induced damage in glacier ice. However, the effects of inherited seismic damage on later warming, especially for the weakening of glacier ice, remain poorly understood. Herein, an event-constrained two-dimensional numerical model is developed based on the 2026 avalanche. An irreversible damage model driven by the historical maximum positive principal elastic strain is proposed and implemented in ABAQUS to investigate glacier ice damage evolution under seismic disturbance, warming, and sequential earthquake–warming loading. Results show that seismic disturbance produces localized damage in the upper glacier and near the ice–rock interface, whereas warming induces more widespread basal damage. The incremental area of severe damage ($$D\ge 0.9$$) exhibits three stages: limited development at warming increments of $$\Delta T<1.4^\circ C$$, earlier development under seismic preconditioning at $$1.4^\circ \text{C}\le \Delta T<4^\circ \text{C}$$, and sustained amplification at $$4^\circ \text{C}\le \Delta T\le 10^\circ \text{C}$$. At $$\Delta T=10^\circ C$$, the model-derived incremental severe damage area reaches approximately 2.6 × 104 m2 with seismic preconditioning, about 3.3 times 7.9 × 103 m2 under warming alone. Moreover, a nearly continuous zone of severe basal damage near the ice–rock interface develops at $$\Delta T=4^\circ \text{C}$$ with seismic pre-disturbance, compared with 8 °C without it. These findings indicate that seismic legacy preferentially intensifies severe damage in previously weakened regions and promotes earlier damage localization under subsequent warming, providing mechanistic insights relevant to climate-related mountain hazard and vulnerability assessment.

item.title: Early–Middle Holocene humid period in the central Mediterranean from speleothem growth at Grotta della Serratura (Southern Italy)
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Zanchetta, Ilaria Isola, Mónica Bini, Giulia Cheli, Hai Cheng, Andrea Columbu, … (+4)
item.description:
Journal of Quaternary Science — matched: Holocene
A phase of speleothem deposition within the Holocene archeological succession of the Serratura Cave (Southern Italy) indicates a period of increasing precipitation in the area. The related increment of cave dripping was probably responsible for the cessation of human occupation in the cave, because of unfavorable conditions. 230 Th/U dating of one flowstone and three stalagmites indicate carbonate deposition from ca. 9.5 to 7.8 ka BP. This interval of growth is in reasonable agreement with a wetter phase identified by δ 18 O record at Corchia Cave and increasing flooding at Renella Cave, both in the Apuan Alps (Central Italy). A review of terrestrial records in peninsular Italy further evidences a wetter Early–Middle Holocene, although lacustrine lake level may suggest different seasonal distribution of rainfall in different areas. However, there are still several open questions concerning the chronology of this wetter interval and its synchronicity over different areas.
